title: The support does not depend on the chosen geometric point
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $x\in X$, and let $\bar x,\bar x'$ be
geometric points of $X$ with image $x$. For every etale sheaf
$F$ on $X_{\Et}$ one has $F_{\bar x}=0$ if and only if
$F_{\bar x'}=0$; consequently the
support of $F$ is independent of the
chosen geometric point over each of its points.

proof.text: Let x be the common image and k = X.residueField x. Take K = SeparableClosure k [def-pd-separable-closure]. Obtain the maps k to Omega and Omega-prime using descResidueField and stalkClosedPointTo, transporting the second along residueFieldCongr for the equality of images [def-weil-geometric-point]. Apply IsAlgClosed.lift [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed] to construct k-algebra embeddings e and e-prime. Put f = Spec(algebraMap k K) followed by fromSpecResidueField x, y = Spec(e), and y-prime = Spec(e-prime). AlgHom.commutes and descResidueField_stalkClosedPointTo_fromSpecResidueField prove y followed by f = s and y-prime followed by f = s-prime.

Let G = Etale.upperStar f applied to F [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. The natural isomorphism Etale.upperStarCompSheafFiberIso [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] identifies its stalks at y and y-prime with the original stalks. K is henselian because it is a field (Field.henselian), and its residue field is isomorphic to K by the bijective residue map, so IsSepClosed.of_ringEquiv makes K strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Spec K is a singleton, so y and y-prime lie over its closed point. Apply strictlyHenselianSections_geometricStalk_isIso [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] twice to identify both stalks of G with its global sections.

Apply Iso.isZero_iff to the two global germ isomorphisms and the two pullback-stalk comparison isomorphisms. Compose the resulting equivalences and rewrite the factorizations from step 1. This proves the simultaneous vanishing assertion with exactly the original hypotheses.
